**Indikator 1** is a central process quality indicator managed by the [[adhd-databasen|ADHD-DATABASEN]] in Denmark. It measures the proportion of ADHD assessment processes—specifically within the [[adhd-udredningspopulation|ADHD-udredningspopulation]]—where a somatic assessment is completed no later than 120 days after the start of the ADHD assessment [^src1] [^src3]. The indicator is critical for ensuring proper differential diagnostics during ADHD evaluations [^src1]. 

The established quality standard and development target for Indikator 1 is ≥ 90% [^src1] [^src3]. Despite its clinical importance, national performance has consistently fallen short of this benchmark, though recent data shows signs of systemic improvement. 

During the 2023/24 reporting period (April 1, 2023, to March 31, 2024), the national average for Indikator 1 was only 59% (95% CI: 58–61) [^src1]. Regional performance varied significantly, with [[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]] at 64%, [[region-syddanmark|Region Syddanmark]] at 62%, [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]] at 64%, [[region-sjaelland|Region Sjælland]] at 60%, and [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland]] struggling at just 36% [^src1]. At the departmental level, only one unit met the 90% standard: [[aabenna-borne-og-ungdomspsykiatrisk-ambulatorium|Aabenraa: Børne og Ungdomspsykiatrisk Ambulatorium]], which achieved exactly 90% (95% CI: 86–93) [^src1]. [[odense-borne-og-ungdomspsykiatrisk-ambulatorium|Odense: Børne- og Ungdomspsykiatrisk Ambulatorium]] narrowly missed the target at 89%, while [[hillerod-psykiatrisk-ambulatorium-boern-og-unge|Hillerød: Psykiatrisk ambulatorium, børn og unge]] reached 81% [^src1].

In the subsequent 2024/25 reporting period (April 1, 2024, to March 31, 2025), the national average improved to 65% (95% CI: 63–66) [^src3]. This marked the first time in several years that the national result had improved compared to the previous counting period [^src4]. Furthermore, four departments managed to reach the development target, which was three more than in the 2023/24 period [^src4]. Regional trends also shifted: [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland]] saw a dramatic increase from 36% to 71%, whereas [[region-sjaelland|Region Sjælland]] experienced a decline from 60% to 49% [^src4]. Despite these localized improvements, the national average of 65% remains well below the 90% development target, highlighting ongoing systemic challenges in completing somatic assessments within the required timeframe [^src3] [^src4].
